content: ZAP Automation Framework auth (zaproxy.org docs, cross-checked with community examples): session handling is declarative config inside a context -- authentication method, a verification strategy (loggedInIndicator/loggedOutIndicator regex against responses, or poll), and session management method (cookie/HTTP-auth). On verification failure, ZAP automatically reruns the login flow to get a fresh session, no manual 'run macro' step. Contrast with Burp's session-handling-rule editor: a rule has a Scope tab (tools/URLs/params) and an Actions tab where you chain 'check session is valid' -> 'run macro' -> 'update cookie jar' by hand per rule; widely blogged as confusing (the 'macro maze'). ZAP's declarative model is the better-designed pattern to copy.
